stories.title: Come Back, Cat!
stories.credit: "Come back, Cat!" written by Nicola Rijsdijk, illustrated by Karen Lilje, (c) Book Dash 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/105115-come-back-cat). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 쪽 하나를 빼고 마지막 쪽에 한 문장을 더했으며, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Come back, cat! Play with me.
Sit in your basket. Stay right here!
Come back, cat! That's way too high.
Come back, cat! Don't go outside.
Come back, cat! That's not yours.
Come back, cat. What have you got?
Come back, cat. That's not your friend!
Hello, cat! Are you back?
Stay in your basket. It's nap time now.
Cat?
There you are, cat. Shh. Nap time.

stories.title: The Bee and the Elephant
stories.credit: "The Bee and the Elephant" by Long Ravy, translated by Celia Bolam, illustrated by Try Samphos, (c) Room to Read 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/37232-the-bee-and-the-elephant). 바꾼 점: 쪽 나눔 그대로, 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: "I am lost," said Little Bee. "I cannot find my home! Can you please help me, Mr. Elephant?"
"Is this nest your home, Little Bee?" the elephant asked.
"Oh no!" cried Little Bee. "This is a bird's home."
"Is this cave your home?" asked the elephant.
"Oh no! This is a bat's home."
"Is this hive your home, Little Bee?"
"Oh yes!" said Little Bee happily. "This is my home."
"Thank you for helping me, Mr. Elephant."

stories.title: The Three Little Kittens
stories.credit: "The Three Little Kittens" by Chou Chinith, translated by Magdalena Cooper, illustrated by Youm Kosal, (c) Room to Read 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/36641-the-three-little-kittens). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: One day three little kittens meet a big dog.
The kittens are scared of the dog.
The little kittens run...
...and the dog follows them.
The little kittens run faster and faster!
The little kittens run into a little bird.
But the little kittens keep on running.
The little kittens run into a little boy.
But the little kittens keep on running.
They run towards a long piece of wood.
"Uh oh! We're in trouble now." "Help! Help!" they cry.
The smiling dog runs up to them. "I'm so happy to run with all of you!" he says.
What a surprise! Now, the little kittens have a new friend.

stories.title: The Race
stories.credit: "The Race" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Kavya Singh and Natasha Mehra, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/12294-the-race). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Four friends want to have a race with their toys.
Veena has a green car. Meena has a yellow auto.
Sanju has a red bus. Manju has a blue lorry.
Ready, one, two, three, go! Here comes Lucky. Ha-ha, Lucky has joined the race.
Look, look! Lucky is the fastest of them all. Lucky wins the race.

stories.title: Fat King Thin Dog
stories.credit: "Fat King Thin Dog" written and illustrated by Parismita, (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/7-fat-king-thin-dog). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 그림 크기를 줄였으며, 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: This is a fat king.
The fat king has a thin dog. The fat king and his thin dog go for a walk.
The dog sees a bird. The dog runs after the bird.
The king runs after the dog.
They run and run. They run and run for many days.
The king catches the dog.
Now the fat king is thin.

stories.title: Ting Tong
stories.credit: "Ting Tong" written by Lubaina Bandukwala, illustrated by Zainab Tambawalla, (c) Pratham Books 2011, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/15458-ting-tong). 바꾼 점: 소리 흉내말의 대문자를 소문자로 바꾸고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Whenever I try to sleep,
Ting tong! The doorbell rings.
Now I turn the other side, and...
Buzz, buzz, the mobile goes.
Once again, I give it a try,
and this time it's a... dong!
Tring, tring! What was that?
A bicycle rushing by!
"What?" says Mamma, seeing me up. "Aren't you asleep still?"
"But Mamma," I tell her with my eyes, "how can I sleep?"
"Ting, buzz, dong, tring! The whole house is full of rings!"

stories.title: Clever Pig
stories.credit: "Clever Pig" written by Nathalie Koenig, illustrated by Josh Morgan, (c) Book Dash 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/19085-clever-pig). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고, 음성 안전검사가 잘못 걸러 낸 6·13·16쪽 문장을 조금 바꾸고(little 추가 등), 글 없는 마지막 두 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Come, Pig! Let's play.
Can you find the carrot?
No, it's not under there.
No, it's not inside.
Clever Pig!
Wake up, little Pig! Let's play. Where did she go?
Pig is gone.
The sun came up.
And the sun went down. But, no Pig.
I miss my friend.
My Pig! Clever Pig.
And one, two, three new friends!
Come, little pigs!
Let's play.
Time for bed!
Good night, little pigs.

stories.title: Counting Animals
stories.credit: "Counting Animals" written by Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi, illustrated by Rob Owen, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/14790-counting-animals). 바꾼 점: 7쪽의 물음 한 문장(사자를 누가 무서워할까?)을 빼고 그림 크기를 줄였으며, 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: One elephant is going to drink water.
Two giraffes are going to drink water.
Three buffaloes and four birds are also going to drink water.
Five antelopes and warthogs are walking to the water.
Seven zebras are running to the water.
Eight frogs and nine fish are swimming in the water.
One lion roars. He also wants to drink.
One elephant is drinking water with the lion.

stories.title: Gorillas Go to the Beach
stories.credit: "Gorillas Go to the Beach" written and illustrated by Jemma Jose, (c) Pratham Books 2019, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/56310-gorillas-go-to-the-beach). 바꾼 점: 'bhutta(인도식 구운 옥수수)'를 'corn'으로 바꾸고 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: The gorillas are off to the beach. Gorillas dig in the sand.
Gorilla jumps in the water. Splash!
Gorilla eats yummy corn from the food carts.
Gorillas throw a frisbee on the shore.
Gorilla plays with a friendly dog.
Gorilla collects shells to show her friends.
Gorillas are tired. Now it's time to watch the moon rise.

stories.title: I Can Climb!
stories.credit: "I Can Climb!" written by Mini Shrinivasan, illustrated by Deval Maniar, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/822-i-can-climb). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I am a big boy now.
I can climb up the steps.
But I cannot climb down again.
I can climb on a chair.
But I cannot climb down again.
I climb on to the chair, and then on the table!
But I cannot climb down again.
"Papa! Papa!" I shout. Papa laughs. "Sonu, learn to climb down!" he says.
I am afraid. But I do not cry.
Slowly, I get down from the table, and down from the chair.
At last, I have learnt to climb down too!

stories.title: Who Is It?
stories.credit: "Who Is It?" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Pratyush Gupta, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/11986-who-is-it). 바꾼 점: 그림이 없는 첫 쪽에는 표지 그림을, 마지막 쪽에는 앞 쪽 그림을 씀, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Priya hears a sound. Srrr... srrr... Who is it?
Priya runs out. She sees the cow chewing grass. No, it is not the cow that is making the sound.
Is it the monkey in the tree? No, it is not the monkey.
Is it the frog hopping in the grass? No, it is not the frog.
Is it the deer jumping along? No, it is not the deer.
Is it the fish in the pond? No, it is not the fish.
Then Priya sees the elephant! The elephant is rubbing its back against a tree.
Now Priya has her answer! Srrr... srrr...

stories.title: The Mango Tree
stories.credit: "The Mango Tree" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Kavya Singh, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/11537-the-mango-tree). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: We like to visit Grandma's village.
Grandma has a big mango tree in her garden. Many birds come there.
I like to hide in the mango tree. No one can see me here.
Father looks for me near the well. Mother looks for me near the cowshed. But no one can find me.
Oh no! At last Grandma's dog finds me.
Now I have to climb down. Grandma gives me a big hug.

stories.title: Piggy Wants to Fly
stories.credit: "Piggy Wants to Fly" by Mut Kunthy, translated by Stephanie Wei, illustrated by Youm Kosal, (c) Room to Read 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/37233-piggy-wants-to-fly). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: "I want to fly like the butterfly does."
"Follow me!" said the butterfly.
"But I do not have wings. I cannot fly."
"I know! I'll use palm leaves to make wings!"
"Flap your wings hard to fly!" cried the butterfly.
"I cannot seem to fly," said Piggy. "Let me try one more time."
"Look! I can fly!" Piggy said, leaping off the branch.
"Oh no! Why did I fall? I do not have wings like you, so I will have to be okay with not flying."

stories.title: Where Is My Bat?
stories.credit: "Where Is My Bat?" by Meera Tendolkar, translated by Madhav Chavan, (c) Pratham Books 2024, illustrated by Kabini Amin, (c) Kabini Amin 2024, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/621383-where-is-my-bat). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I have lost my bat, and I cannot find it.
I looked behind the door. It was not there.
I looked for it on the shelf. I could not find it there.
I looked for it under the bed. Not there either.
I searched inside the box. There was no sign of it.
I searched the attic. I could not find it anywhere. I looked here, there and everywhere.
Oh! There's my bat!

stories.title: Lost and Found
stories.credit: "Lost and Found" written and illustrated by Sukhada Rahalkar, (c) Pratham Books 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/356-lost-and-found). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Not here, not there. Where have you gone?
Not on the sofa. Not under the cot.
Not in the box. Not under my sister's frock.
Not under the pillow. Not in my bag. Sob, sob, where have you gone?
I have looked in every room. I have looked under every book.
I have looked under the chair. I have looked under the stool. Where have you gone?
Soon Granny came back from her walk. "Look what I found in the park."
"It can sway, it can bounce. It can spin, it can dangle. Ha-ha, hee-hee," said Granny with a giggle.
Oh Granny! Thank you so much! You have found my dear yo-yo!
"Yo-yo? What a funny name! What a funny toy! I want to play with it. It gives me so much joy!"
Giggle, giggle, giggling away, Granny played with my little toy for the rest of the day!

stories.title: Look at Me
stories.credit: "Look at Me" by Pankaj Chaturvedi, translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Ajit Narayan, (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/184-look-at-me). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Look at us. Do you want to be our friend?
My legs are very strong. I can run really fast with them.
And my arms... such a nice swing!
I like to draw. I use my hands for drawing.
Should I draw your picture? I can see you with my eyes.
The bird sings a sweet song. I can hear it with my ears.
I think Ma is making halwa. I can smell it with my nose.
Oh! This sugarcane is so tough! But my teeth are strong too!
It is very sweet. My tongue just told me.
I can sing. Should I sing you a song?
Ma says I have a good voice. Does it come from my throat?

stories.title: Who Is Our Friend?
stories.credit: "Who Is Our Friend?" written by Jade Mathieson, illustrated by Gerhard Van Wyk, (c) Book Dash 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/24795-who-is-our-friend). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 글 없는 쪽을 뺐으며, 음성 안전검사가 잘못 걸러 낸 두 문장(벼룩을 먹는다·쪼아 청소한다)을 'picks them all off', 'cleans them all'로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Can you guess who our best friend is? He's not like us at all.
Our best friend is Bird!
I am Rhino. I get covered in fleas.
Bird picks them all off.
I am Crocodile. I can't brush my teeth.
Bird cleans them all.
I am Giraffe. I can't scratch my head.
Bird can reach just the right spot.
I am Zebra. I can't see things far away.
Bird has great eyes, so when he's watching, I'm safe.
Bird might be different, but that's no problem...
We don't even mind when he sings!
Will you be my friend?

stories.title: Tumi Goes to the Park
stories.credit: "Tumi Goes to the Park" written by Paballo Rampa, illustrated by Nyambura Kariuki, (c) Book Dash 2017, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/18402-tumi-goes-to-the-park). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 글 없는 쪽 4개를 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: It's Tumi's first trip to the park.
"Mama, what's that?"
"It's a slide," says Mama. "May I go on it?" asks Tumi. "Of course!" says Mama.
"Wheeeee!"
"Look, Mama, I swing like a monkey."
"I just went past you ten times, Mama!" says Tumi. "Clever girl!" says Mama. "You know how to count!"
"Do you want to play?" asks Tumi. "Yes!" says the boy.
"I'm Tumi." "I'm Zakhe."
Tumi sees the sandpit. "Let's build a sandcastle!" says Tumi.
"I'm taking a photo for Gogo," says Mama.
"It's time to go home now, Tumi," says Mama. "Bye, Zakhe!" waves Tumi. "Bye, Tumi!" says Zakhe. "See you next time!"
"Mama, thank you for bringing me to the park," says Tumi.

stories.title: Rat and Goat
stories.credit: "Rat and Goat" by Ley Sorya, translated by Sanjana Khoobchandani, illustrated by Try Samphors, (c) Room to Read 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/36678-rat-and-goat). 바꾼 점: 캄보디아 놀이 이름 'Moek'을 빼고 'hopscotch'만 남겼으며, 글 없는 쪽 2개를 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Rat loves to play outside.
Today he wants to play hopscotch, but there is nobody to play with.
"I have an idea," he thinks. "I'll invite Goat, my neighbour."
Goat likes to spend time alone, fishing and napping.
Rat goes to Goat's house and knocks on the door. Tok, tok!
"Brother Goat!" Rat exclaims. "Come play with me!"
"No, no!" Goat says. "I need to sleep. I don't want to play."
"Please, Goat," Rat replies. "Play with me. We will have fun together."
Finally, Goat agrees. "Okay, okay," Goat says. "I will play with you."
Goat and Rat play hopscotch together.
Goat has lots of fun playing with Rat. He decides that next time, he will jump out of bed to play.

stories.title: My Best Friend
stories.credit: "My Best Friend" written by Anupa Lal, illustrated by Suvidha Mistry, (c) Pratham Books 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/1042-my-best-friend). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I have a friend. She lives in my house.
When I am happy, so is she.
When I cry, she cries too.
But I cannot hear her voice. My friend lives inside the mirror.
"Come out," I tell her, "we will play." She does not come out.
I am not happy. I go to sleep.
She comes out of the mirror in my sleep! And we have fun.
We play, we run, we shout and scream together.
When I talk to her, she also talks to me.
In the morning, my friend will go back into the mirror.
But I don't mind at all. We will play again in my dreams!

stories.title: I Can Help!
stories.credit: "I Can Help!" written by Mini Shrinivasan, illustrated by Aman Randhawa, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/968-i-can-help). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I am a big girl. I can help other people.
After school, I like to feed my brother. He loves it.
When I have a holiday, I help my mother to get ready to go to the office.
In the evening, I help my father in his shop.
But sometimes my mother says, "Please, do not help me!"
And sometimes my father says, "Thank you, but please do not help me today."
Sometimes they both tell me to sit in one place. I like to read a book then!
I like to help my grandmother. She tells me stories.
My brother is still small. He cannot help at all.
But I am a big girl.
I can help other people.

stories.title: Is There Anyone Like Me?
stories.credit: "Is There Anyone Like Me?" written by Fred Strydom, illustrated by Jess Jardim-Wedepohl, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/15136-is-there-anyone-like-me). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I wonder if there's another me somewhere in the world.
Who looks the same.
And talks the same.
And even has my curls.
Someone with my eyes, my ears.
Who even has my laugh.
Who can do what I can do.
And can't do what I can't.
I've looked and looked everywhere to find another me. I went down to the park and looked behind the trees.
I looked around, up and down.
At every single face.
I couldn't find another me in any single place.
There's only one me in the world! I'm special, oh it's true!
But not just me, don't you see? There's only one of you!

stories.title: The Moon and the Cap
stories.credit: Adapted from "The Moon and The Cap" by Rohini Nilekani, illustrated by Angie & Upesh, (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0 (storyweaver.org.in). 아이 눈높이로 문장을 고쳐 썼고 그림은 bilody가 새로 그림.

pages.text: Look. A cap. A blue cap. Mama gives me a blue cap. I put on my cap. My cap is soft and blue. I like my blue cap.
Oh! The wind blows. Whoosh, whoosh. The wind is strong. The wind takes my cap. Up, up, up. Where is my cap? Whoosh goes the wind.
Look. A tree. A big tall tree. My cap is up in the tree. The tree holds my cap. My cap sits in the tree.
It is night. Look up. The moon. A bright moon. The moon sees my cap. The moon smiles. Do you see the moon? Hello, moon.
The moon puts on my cap. Look. The moon has a blue cap. The cap fits the moon. A happy moon. I smile at the moon.
Look. A new cap. A red cap. Mama says it is from the moon. Now I have a cap. The moon has a cap. Good night, moon.

stories.title: Who Can?
stories.credit: Adapted from "Can and Can't" by Radha HS, illustrated by Ruchi Shah, (c) Pratham Books 2010, CC BY 4.0 (storyweaver.org.in). 아이 눈높이로 문장을 고쳐 썼고 그림은 bilody가 새로 그림.

pages.text: Look. A fish. A little fish. The fish can swim. Swim, swim, swim. The fish swims and swims. Do you see the fish?
Look up. A bird. A little blue bird. The bird can fly. Fly, fly, fly. Up and up goes the bird.
Look. A dog. A happy dog. The dog can bark. Woof, woof. The dog can run too. Run, run, little dog.
Look. A cat. A soft cat. The cat can jump. Jump, jump. Up jumps the cat. What a big jump, little cat.
Look. A monkey. A funny monkey. The monkey can swing. Swing, swing, swing. Hold on, little monkey.
Look. A pig. A pink pig. The pig can eat. Yum, yum, yum. And I can clap. Clap, clap, clap. Bye-bye, little pig.

intro.text: Hi! It is story time. Look and listen with me.

end.text: The end. That was fun. Bye-bye!

next.text: The end! Here comes another story.
